## Unified transport acceptance boundaries

Public API 1.0.0 uses one renderer, at most 32 voices and capacity for 1-4 sequences. `bus` categories and per-voice sends share one effects chain. These API changes do not establish complete multiplatform ten-minute maximum-load acceptance; the measured iPad result and Android limits are recorded separately in [physical validation](../docs/validation/physical-validation.json) and [the performance summary](stats-performance.md). Host timing, bypass comparisons, memory accounting, actual Android/iOS builds and the remaining device/listening checks are separate evidence. The cited Studio and unified-transport benchmarks are historical observations. In the pre-variation layout, effects buffers at 192 kHz used approximately 13.1 MiB and four maximum-size triple-bank transports used 8,627,712 bytes (8.23 MiB), excluding renderer voices and queues. The local 1.1.0 candidate grows those four transports to 9,537,152 bytes (9.10 MiB) on the measured 64-bit macOS layout, an increase of 909,440 bytes; see [variation storage measurements](native-variation-validation.md#storage-and-callback-work). These structure sizes are not a new whole-process or physical-device measurement. Total accounting must also include renderer voices/tails, command queues, effects, bridge/canonical options and recovery peaks. The 32 MiB additional-memory target remains a target, not a certified bound for the candidate.

The current diagnostics add `preLimiterPeakDb` (maximum signal before final limiting, in dBFS) and `maxLimiterReductionDb` (greatest limiter attenuation in dB) accumulated since reset. ## Holding a sound and adding movement

Choose a held voice when the ending follows a player action instead of a fixed duration: motor, charge beam, pad or the last chord of a ceremony. `noteOn` starts a positive app-owned ID; `noteOff` begins release from the current level, and compatible `updateVoice` edits ramp over 10 ms. Distinct IDs remain independent events with fixed gain. Reserve enough capacity for their releases and unrelated effects, and release on cancellation as well as ordinary key up. See the [held motor recipe](examples.md#sustained-game-motor) for retry/cleanup handling.

A fanfare can use beat or millisecond sequences with native chords, rests, gate, independent length, swing and pitch-ordered arpeggios. A long release can ring over later steps. Use held voices when release follows presentation or interaction. See [transport usage](guide.md#choose-the-musical-transport).

The two additional voice LFOs move filter cutoff, square PWM or sine FM index using sine/triangle shapes. Cutoff movement creates slow breathing or rhythmic filtering; PWM adds changing harmonic color; a small FM-index modulation varies brightness. Free rates reach 20 Hz, and synced rates follow native transport tempo. These slots are separate from pitch vibrato. Avoid deep/high-rate modulation with strong resonance or high-frequency FM; safe parameter clamping does not guarantee a pleasant or alias-free sound. The [two-LFO example](examples.md#two-voice-lfos) shows a filtered PWM pad.

The panel shows active/peak/spatial/tail voices, pending commands, replacements, request/publication rejections, priority drops, callback load, stereo output peak and backend underruns. ## Native attack variation

The **ATTACK VARIATION** button submits the same metal-strike recipe on each press. With `capabilities.variation === true` and `variationSchemaVersion === 1`, the renderer chooses pitch, FM depth and level once per admitted attack. Older packages receive the original recipe without the dictionary. This button uses independent timed events; the [variation guide](../documentation/native-variation.md) separately demonstrates sustained ownership and native sequence retriggers. Physical listening acceptance remains separate from host correctness checks.

## Implementation and verification

Both renderers use [`shared/synth_variation.h`](../shared/synth_variation.h): stable schema slots, integer-defined SplitMix64 finalization and exact uint32-to-uniform conversion. Parsing prepares a fixed 144-byte configuration outside the audio callback. The callback performs bounded arithmetic without allocation, locks, JavaScript calls or entropy services.

Focused checks cover known vectors, both native validators, attack admission, chord ordinals, sustained stability, loops, revisions, rejection and old-renderer compatibility with controlled noise initialization. [Technical verification](native-variation-validation.md) records the measured memory/callback cost and its limits. Host results do not certify physical latency or listening quality on every device.
